origin.objective_verbatim: Explore friction and how it can be helpful or unhelpful. Investigate mechanisms: levers, pulleys and gears. Plan and carry out a fair test about forces; record results. Describe the movement of the Earth and other planets around the Sun. Describe the movement of the Moon around the Earth.

outcome: I can explain familiar science using an observation, model or genuine piece of work.

routes.choice: For each of the four supplied science decisions, choose the matching evidence card rather than an unrelated card. In your book, give one short reason for each choice, using the printed because stem.
routes.aspire_text: AspireExplain each decision and qualify a model or data claim.Help with Autumn ScienceIdentify what the evidence supports and one thing it cannot show.
routes.independent: Answer the four decisions and support each with a science reason.
routes.supported: Use prepared cards for friction, a lever, a fair comparison and Moonlight.Help with Autumn SciencePoint to the evidence, then finish one because statement.Small supported promptsHelp with Autumn ScienceName the touching surfaces; gain and cost; control; light or orbit cause.

must_know_words: a force opposing sliding or attempted sliding between touching surfaces
the point a lever turns around
something kept the same in a comparison
a curved path around another body
method_steps: Select the familiar evidence cards for the four science decisions.
Identify which observation belongs to each decision. Stop and check the task and agreed support with the adult.
Keep a first answer and use only the permitted support, with no new practical required.
In your book, record the evidence, a scientific conclusion and one checked improvement.
P17_staff_support: Give time to start → point to the relevant place → rephrase → offer a small prompt or word bank → reduce to a limited choice. Never straight to telling the answer.
P18: Retained existing target placeholders and opportunities in lesson Guidance.

teacher_questions.1: How can an observation support a familiar science explanation?
teacher_questions.2: Where does friction help, and where can it hinder?
teacher_questions.3: Two accounts say “it went farther”; which account lets us explain why?
teacher_questions.4: What can the supplied comparison data support, and what can they not show?
teacher_questions.6: How can a lever reduce effort force without creating energy?
teacher_questions.7: Which science idea explains each evidence card?
teacher_questions.8: What evidence supports each of your four science decisions?
teacher_questions.9: Which decision became clearer after you checked the evidence?
teacher_questions.10: Which answer did you improve, and why?
